title: Grain Still Owed under Grain Marketing Contracts Set against an Arrears Settlement, Crop Input Purchasing Accounts
content:
A member who still owes the cooperative bushels under Grain Marketing Contracts has part of the value of that grain set against what is sought to settle the arrears on their crop input account, and how much follows whether the cooperative has already issued them a settlement statement on their grain.

Where the member has bushels still owed to the cooperative on a live grain marketing contract and a settlement statement has been issued to them on their grain over the 10 statement months before the handling date, the share set against the amount sought is 25 percent. Where the member has bushels still owed on a live grain marketing contract and no settlement statement has been issued to them on their grain over those months, the share set against the amount sought is 10 percent. In every other case no share of the value of the grain still owed is set against the amount sought on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts.

The value the share is taken on is the bushels still owed on that live contract multiplied by the cash price the contract carries. A member with no bushels still owed carries no such credit whatever settlement statements stand on their grain, and a member holding no live grain marketing contract carries none either.

*Worked on hypothetical figures.* A member still owes 6000 bushels on a live grain marketing contract carrying a cash price of 4.20 USD the bushel, a value of 25200.00 USD. Where a settlement statement has been issued to them on their grain inside the window, 25 percent of that value, being 6300.00 USD, is set against the amount sought; where none has been issued inside the window, 10 percent of it, being 2520.00 USD, is set against the amount sought.
